title: Dasakam 12: Varaha Avataram
description: Manu's concern over the submerged Earth leads Brahma to seek the Lord; the divine boar Varaha grows, descends into the waters, and raises the Earth.

source.commentary: intake/D012/photo-captions.txt; original source and retrieval metadata preserved in content/sources/d012/

stanzas.sanskrit:
स्वायम्भुवो मनुरथो जनसर्गशीलो
दृष्ट्वा महीमसमये सलिले निमग्नाम् ।
स्रष्टारमाप शरणं भवदङ्घ्रिसेवा-
-तुष्टाशयं मुनिजनैः सह सत्यलोके ॥ १२-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
svāyambhuvo manuratho janasargaśīlo
dṛṣṭvā mahīmasamaye salile nimagnām |
sraṣṭāramāpa śaraṇaṃ bhavadaṅghrisevā-
-tuṣṭāśayaṃ munijanaiḥ saha satyaloke || 12-1 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Svāyambhuva Manu, intent on creating beings, saw the Earth submerged in water at an untimely hour. With sages he sought refuge with Brahmā in Satyaloka, whose heart was content in serving Your feet.
stanzas.commentary_en: Swayambhu Manu, Son of Brahma started creating the species on earth. Suddenly he noticed that Earth was floating in water, even though there was no pralaya. Immediately he went to satyaloka, along with other sages and surrendered to Brahma who remains blissful  on the Lotus feet of Bhagwan.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कष्टं प्रजाः सृजति मय्यवनिर्निमग्ना
स्थानं सरोजभव कल्पय तत्प्रजानाम् ।
इत्येवमेष कथितो मनुना स्वयम्भू-
-रम्भोरुहाक्ष तव पादयुगं व्यचिन्तीत् ॥ १२-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kaṣṭaṃ prajāḥ sṛjati mayyavanirnimagnā
sthānaṃ sarojabhava kalpaya tatprajānām |
ityevameṣa kathito manunā svayambhū-
-rambhoruhākṣa tava pādayugaṃ vyacintīt || 12-2 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Manu told the self-born Brahmā, “The Earth is submerged while I create beings; alas, provide a place for them.” Thus addressed, Brahmā contemplated Your pair of feet, O lotus-eyed Lord.
stanzas.commentary_en: Swayambu Manu requested Brahma to give a place to put the species created by him, as the earth was sinking in the water. Brahma contemplated and surrendered at the lotus feet of Bhagwan.

stanzas.sanskrit:
हा हा विभो जलमहं न्यपिबं पुरस्ता-
-दद्यापि मज्जति मही किमहं करोमि ।
इत्थं त्वदङ्घ्रियुगलं शरणं यतोऽस्य
नासापुटात् समभवः शिशुकोलरूपी ॥ १२-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hā hā vibho jalamahaṃ nyapibaṃ purastā-
-dadyāpi majjati mahī kimahaṃ karomi |
itthaṃ tvadaṅghriyugalaṃ śaraṇaṃ yato'sya
nāsāpuṭāt samabhavaḥ śiśukolarūpī || 12-3 ||
stanzas.translation_en: “Alas, Lord! I drank the waters before, yet the Earth is sinking again. What shall I do?” Taking refuge in Your feet, Brahmā spoke; then from his nostril You appeared in the form of an infant boar.
stanzas.commentary_en: Brahma took refuge at Bhagwan’s lotus feet saying that HE had earlier also drunk the waters and that the earth was still submerging and he did not know what to do. From Brahma’s nostrils, Bhagwan emerged in the form of a child boar.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रवपुरुत्पतितः पुरस्ता-
-द्भूयोऽथ कुम्भिसदृशः समजृम्भथास्त्वम् ।
अभ्रे तथाविधमुदीक्ष्य भवन्तमुच्चै-
-र्विस्मेरतां विधिरगात् सह सूनुभिः स्वैः ॥ १२-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aṅguṣṭhamātravapurutpatitaḥ purastā-
-dbhūyo'tha kumbhisadṛśaḥ samajṛmbhathāstvam |
abhre tathāvidhamudīkṣya bhavantamuccai-
-rvismeratāṃ vidhiragāt saha sūnubhiḥ svaiḥ || 12-4 ||
stanzas.translation_en: At first You rose only thumb-sized; then You expanded to the size of an elephant. Seeing Your immense form in the sky, Brahmā and his sons were filled with wonder.
stanzas.commentary_en: At first the size of the boar was like the size of a thumb, then it gradually grew to the size of an elephant. Brahma and his sons were wonder struck seeing the huge form in the sky.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कोऽसावचिन्त्यमहिमा किटिरुत्थितो मे
नासापुटात् किमु भवेदजितस्य माया ।
इत्थं विचिन्तयति धातरि शैलमात्रः
सद्यो भवन् किल जगर्जिथ घोरघोरम् ॥ १२-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ko'sāvacintyamahimā kiṭirutthito me
nāsāpuṭāt kimu bhavedajitasya māyā |
itthaṃ vicintayati dhātari śailamātraḥ
sadyo bhavan kila jagarjitha ghoraghoram || 12-5 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Brahmā wondered, “Who is this boar of inconceivable majesty that arose from my nostril? Could this be the unconquered Lord's Māyā?” As the Creator pondered, You at once grew mountain-sized and roared terribly.
stanzas.commentary_en: Brahma was wondering as to who the glorious boar was which had come out from his nostrils. As he was trying to reflect if it was the work of the Invincible Maya, Bhagwan in the form of the boar became the size of a mountain and roared fiercely.

stanzas.sanskrit:
तं ते निनादमुपकर्ण्य जनस्तपःस्थाः
सत्यस्थिताश्च मुनयो नुनुवुर्भवन्तम् ।
तत् स्तोत्रहर्षुलमनाः परिणद्य भूय-
-स्तोयाशयं विपुलमूर्तिरवातरस्त्वम् ॥ १२-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
taṃ te ninādamupakarṇya janastapaḥsthāḥ
satyasthitāśca munayo nunuvurbhavantam |
tat stotraharṣulamanāḥ pariṇadya bhūya-
-stoyāśayaṃ vipulamūrtiravātarastvam || 12-6 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Hearing Your roar, sages dwelling in Jana, Tapa, and Satya praised You. Delighted by their hymn, You roared again and, in a vast form, descended into the ocean.
stanzas.commentary_en: The fierce roaring sound reached the Jana, Tapa and Satya lokas and the sages began to sing in praise of Bhagwan in the form of Varaha murthy. The pleased Bhagwan roared once again happily and jumped in to the ocean, searching for the Goddess Earth.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वप्रसारिपरिधूम्रविधूतरोमा
प्रोत्क्षिप्तवालधिरवाङ्मुखघोरघोणः ।
तूर्णप्रदीर्णजलदः परिघूर्णदक्ष्णा
स्तोतॄन्मुनीन् शिशिरयन्नवतेरिथ त्वम् ॥ १२-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ūrdhvaprasāriparidhūmravidhūtaromā
protkṣiptavāladhiravāṅmukhaghoraghoṇaḥ |
tūrṇapradīrṇajaladaḥ parighūrṇadakṣṇā
stotṝnmunīn śiśirayannavateritha tvam || 12-7 ||
stanzas.translation_en: With bristling dusky hairs, tail raised, fierce snout pointing downward, and rolling eyes, You swiftly tore through the clouds. Cooling the praising sages with Your glance, You plunged below.
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord Varaha had tail lifted up with reddish and black hair standing erect, had a fierce looking nose, pointed down and rolling eyes. With face slightly bent so as to bless the praising sages, Varaha broke through the clouds and jumped in to the ocean.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अन्तर्जलं तदनु सङ्कुलनक्रचक्रं
भ्राम्यत्तिमिङ्गिलकुलं कलुषोर्मिमालम् ।
आविश्य भीषणरवेण रसातलस्था-
-नाकम्पयन् वसुमतीमगवेषयस्त्वम् ॥ १२-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
antarjalaṃ tadanu saṅkulanakracakraṃ
bhrāmyattimiṅgilakulaṃ kaluṣormimālam |
āviśya bhīṣaṇaraveṇa rasātalasthā-
-nākampayan vasumatīmagaveṣayastvam || 12-8 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Entering the waters crowded with circling crocodiles, roaming whales, and murky ranks of waves, You searched for the Earth, making the denizens of Rasātala tremble with Your terrible roar.
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord Varaha entered the insides of the waters where the crocodiles and whales were whirling around and which was full of turbulent waves. The inhabitants of Rasatala shook with fear as with a fierce roar Lord Varaha searched for the earth.

stanzas.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वाऽथ दैत्यहतकेन रसातलान्ते
संवेशितां झटिति कूटकिटिर्विभो त्वम् ।
आपातुकानविगणय्य सुरारिखेटान्
दंष्ट्राङ्कुरेण वसुधामदधाः सलीलम् ॥ १२-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dṛṣṭvā'tha daityahatakena rasātalānte
saṃveśitāṃ jhaṭiti kūṭakiṭirvibho tvam |
āpātukānavigaṇayya surārikheṭān
daṃṣṭrāṅkureṇa vasudhāmadadhāḥ salīlam || 12-9 ||
stanzas.translation_en: Seeing the Earth hidden at the edge of Rasātala by the wicked demon, You, O Lord in boar form, paid no heed to the approaching demon hordes and playfully supported the Earth on the tip of Your tusk.
stanzas.commentary_en: Then seeing the earth concealed by the Asura at the bottom of the Rasatala, Lord Varaha lifted it up with the tip of the tusk of the boar. This was like a mere sport for Lord Varaha.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अभ्युद्धरन्नथ धरां दशनाग्रलग्न-
-मुस्ताङ्कुराङ्कित इवाधिकपीवरात्मा ।
उद्धूतघोरसलिलाज्जलधेरुदञ्चन्
क्रीडावराहवपुरीश्वर पाहि रोगात् ॥ १२-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
abhyuddharannatha dharāṃ daśanāgralagna-
-mustāṅkurāṅkita ivādhikapīvarātmā |
uddhūtaghorasalilājjaladherudañcan
krīḍāvarāhavapurīśvara pāhi rogāt || 12-10 ||
stanzas.translation_en: As You raised the Earth, it clung to the tip of Your tusk like a tiny sprout of nut-grass upon Your immense body. Rising from the ocean that You had churned up, O Lord whose playful form is the boar, protect me from illness.
stanzas.commentary_en:
The gigantic earth looked like a blade of grass stuck to the tip of the tooth of Lord Varaha.
Bhattathiri requested Lord Guruvayoorappan, who with his Maya took the form of Varaha and saved the Earth from sinking in ocean, to eradicate his ailments.
